summary: The prepared source already contains an issue-specific SWA admission escape hatch. When a request budget cannot fit the total SWA pool, PrefillAdder computes a page-aligned safe chunk and admits it instead of indefinitely deferring the FCFS queue head. A new regression using the reported 20,992-token pool, 32,768-token chunk limit, 512-token page, and 20,742-token prompt demonstrates NO_TOKEN with the old behavior simulated and progress with the current implementation (19,968 tokens admitted). No production source correction was justified.

gpu_execution_evidence: The verified defect and existing correction are deterministic scheduler admission arithmetic and do not execute GPU kernels. HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 restricted the test process to the assigned device, but the unit path remained CPU-only.
remaining_limitations: DeepSeek-V4-Pro/DSpark weights and the reported 1P1D TP4+TP4, 8xB300 deployment were unavailable, so no full-model HTTP or distributed reproduction is claimed.

The regression verifies scheduler admission and FCFS-head progress with the exact reported pool/chunk/page/prompt geometry; it does not validate DeepSeek-V4 semantic output, mooncake transfer, or multi-node behavior.
The current implementation resolves the hang by safely chunking an intrinsically oversized prefill rather than returning the suggested HTTP 400.
